title: Socioeconomic Context of Melanoma Patients in Lower Saxony and Germany
summary:
Socioeconomic factors such as income, education, and living environment are known to influence health outcomes. For many types of cancer, studies have shown that people living in socially disadvantaged regions are more likely to be diagnosed at a later stage and have poorer survival. However, for malignant melanoma, one of the most common skin cancers, comprehensive data addressing these inequalities in Germany are still lacking.
The aim of this study is to investigate whether socioeconomic status and place of residence influence the stage at diagnosis, access to treatment, and survival of patients with malignant melanoma. For this purpose, existing pseudonymized data from the Clinical Cancer Registry of Lower Saxony and the ADOReg registry will be analyzed. No new data collection or additional examinations of patients are required.
Socioeconomic status will be determined based on patients’ postal code using an established deprivation index and linked to clinical information such as tumor stage, treatment course, and mortality. The results are intended to improve understanding of socioeconomic inequalities in melanoma care and to support the development of targeted support measures for particularly vulnerable patient groups.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients documented in the KKN or ADOReg with malignant melanoma (ICD-10 C43)
Fully pseudonymized datasets
Exclusion criteria:
Missing or incomplete registry data on place of residence, diagnosis, or tumor stage
Inability to analyze postal code assignment
